Done. Two files changed:

**`src/main/resources/db/migration/V4__widen_idempotency_key.sql`** (new)
```sql
ALTER TABLE payment ALTER COLUMN idempotency_key TYPE VARCHAR(128);
```

**`src/main/java/mn/pay/Payment.java:14`** — `@Column(nullable = false, length = 128)` on `idempotencyKey`. It previously had no `length`, so the mapping implied Hibernate's default 255 while the table said 64; pinning it to 128 makes the entity and the schema agree at the new width.

Those were the only two spots. The GraphQL `idempotencyKey: String!` and `PaymentValidator.check` impose no length at all (only non-blank), so nothing there needed widening.

Three things worth knowing:

- **Your checkout is stale.** HEAD is detached at `d599b0b`, five commits behind `origin/main`. On main the package is renamed `mn.pay` → `mn.payments`, everything has been reformatted, and migrations `V2__payment_unique_index.sql` / `V3__drop_unused_indexes.sql` exist. I numbered the new file **V4** rather than V2 so it doesn't collide when this lands on main — but the `Payment.java` edit is against the old path and will need replaying onto `mn/payments/Payment.java`. Say the word and I'll redo the change on a branch off `main` instead.
- **I added a new migration rather than editing `V1__init.sql`'s `VARCHAR(64)`**, since V1 has shipped and has two migrations layered on top of it; rewriting it would break Flyway checksums on any environment that already ran it.
- **Flyway isn't a declared dependency** in `pom.xml` (nor on main), so nothing in the app applies `db/migration/*.sql` at startup — these files are currently applied by some path outside this repo. The widening only takes effect wherever that process runs. The `ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE` syntax follows PostgreSQL, matching V3's use of `pg_stat_user_indexes`.

`mvn -o -DskipTests compile` passes.
